paper.title: Altruistic punishment in humans
paper.research_question: Whether costly punishment of defectors promotes cooperation among anonymous strangers when reputation and direct reciprocity are ruled out.
paper.setting: Anonymous public goods experiment with random rematching and real monetary stakes.

game_context.baseline_condition: No-punishment public goods game: simultaneous contributions, then contribution feedback, no sanction stage.

mechanisms.name: Altruistic peer punishment of defectors
mechanisms.summary: After observing group members' contributions, each subject can pay to reduce another member's payoff. Punishment is costly to the punisher, yields no direct material gain, and is mainly directed at below-average contributors, increasing cooperation.

actors.decision_maker: Each group member after contribution feedback
actors.target: Other group members, especially below-average contributors
actors.observer: Participants observe contributions, not identities; punishment decisions are simultaneous

information_structure.anonymity: Anonymous; identities not revealed; no subject met another more than once
public_information: Other group members' contributions after contribution stage
information_structure.history_visibility: No reputation formation; limited own past experience across periods

action_space_changes.condition: Available after observing contributions in punishment treatment

payoff_changes.condition: For each point received from another member

state_variables.name: punishment_points_sent
state_variables.update_rule: Record points each agent assigns to each other agent after contributions

state_variables.name: punishment_points_received
state_variables.update_rule: Sum points received by each agent in the punishment stage

state_variables.name: punishment_cost
state_variables.update_rule: Subtract 1 MU times points sent from punisher payoff

state_variables.name: punishment_penalty
state_variables.update_rule: Subtract 3 MUs times points received from target payoff

state_variables.name: deviation_from_others_average_contribution
state_variables.update_rule: Agent contribution minus average contribution of the other group members

prompt_requirements: Tell agents they may assign 0-10 punishment points to each other group member after seeing contributions.
State that each point costs the punisher 1 MU and reduces the target payoff by 3 MUs.
State anonymity and lack of future interaction/reputation if modeled.

metrics.name: mean_contribution
metrics.definition: Average contribution to the public good by period and treatment

metrics.name: punishment_frequency
metrics.definition: Count or fraction of positive punishment assignments

metrics.name: punishment_by_negative_deviation
metrics.definition: Punishment received as a function of falling below others' average contribution

metrics.name: net_payoff
metrics.definition: Public goods payoff minus punishment costs and penalties

minimal_code_changes: Add post-contribution punishment action for each ordered pair of distinct group members.
Reveal round contributions before punishment decisions.
Apply payoff update: sender cost=points, target penalty=3*points.
Log punishment matrix, contribution deviations, and cooperation metrics.
risks_or_assumptions: Baseline may not support multi-stage rounds or pairwise actions.
LLM agents may require clear prompts to avoid confusion between contribution and punishment stages.
If identities/history persist, reputation effects may confound punishment.

experiment_design.baseline_condition: Anonymous stranger public goods game without punishment.
treatment_conditions: Anonymous stranger public goods game with post-contribution costly punishment.

cooperation_outcomes: Punishment occurred frequently: 84.3% punished at least once; 34.3% punished more than five times.
74.2% of punishment acts were imposed on below-average contributors by above-average contributors.
Average cooperation was much higher with punishment than without punishment in both treatment orders.
In final punishment period, 38.9% contributed all 20 MUs and 77.8% contributed at least 15 MUs.
In final no-punishment period, 58.9% contributed nothing and 75.6% contributed 5 MUs or less.
evidence.reported_effect_direction: Punishment strongly increased and sustained cooperation; cooperation declined without punishment.
evidence.reported_effect_size: A 10 MU negative deviation from others' average contribution increased others' punishment expenditure by 6.22 MUs, imposing an 18.66 MU payoff reduction.
key_quotes_or_passages: Cooperation flourishes if altruistic punishment is possible, and breaks down if it is ruled out.
Each point assigned cost the punished member 3 MUs and the punishing member 1 MU.
The punishment of non-cooperators substantially increased the amount that subjects invested in the public good.
